about: The real code blaze is judged on (AGENTS.md rule verify-on-real-projects; pins.py reads it). `crates`: top crates of crates.io for corpus.py, each pinned, fetched from static.crates.io as its .crate, checked against the sparse index's cksum, and its own tests run by `blaze test` and judged by their own verdicts; chosen so that no test needs the network, a service, trybuild or a rustc of its own; versions the newest unyanked release on 2026-10-29. `workspaces`: whole workspaces for realprojects.py, each at a commit and that commit's git tree id (looked up on GitHub on 2026-11-03), built with `blaze build --workspace --all-targets` and tested with `blaze test --workspace`; where blaze_cli.py pins the same project it pins the same commit.

workspaces.name: blaze
workspaces.why: blaze builds blaze (rule blaze-builds-blaze): this repository at the run's commit, exported with git archive

workspaces.name: ripgrep
workspaces.why: a mid-size workspace with a build script, integration tests that run the binary, and blaze_cli.py's pin; its tests run in blaze's sandbox (`sandboxed-tests`)

workspaces.name: nushell
workspaces.why: 40-odd crates, heavy proc macros (nu-protocol derives) and a large test suite; blaze_cli.py's pin

workspaces.name: helix
workspaces.why: an editor with tree-sitter's C code built by build scripts; the grammars' own fetch and build is off as blaze_cli.py has it

workspaces.name: wasmtime
workspaces.why: a JIT (Cranelift) and its spec test suite from submodules; debug info off as blaze_cli.py has it (8.5 GB of target with it)

workspaces.name: rust-analyzer
workspaces.why: salsa, deep generics and expect-test snapshots; blaze_cli.py's pin

workspaces.name: cargo
workspaces.why: cargo's workspace; its testsuite runs the cargo it built, never a host cargo; blaze_cli.py's cargo-lib pin

workspaces.name: bevy
workspaces.why: an ECS with heavy generics, derive macros and trait-object plumbing; on Linux its build scripts need alsa, udev, wayland and xkbcommon's headers (realprojects.yaml installs them)

workspaces.name: tokio
workspaces.why: the async runtime: atomics, unsafe, macros; `full` as tokio's CI tests it

workspaces.name: serde
workspaces.why: serde and serde_derive with test_suite's derive cases

workspaces.name: rayon
workspaces.why: work stealing, threads, unwinding across them

workspaces.name: regex
workspaces.why: regex, regex-automata and regex-syntax with their large TOML-driven test suites

workspaces.name: hyper
workspaces.why: HTTP on tokio, tests over loopback sockets; `full` as hyper's CI tests it

workspaces.name: polars
workspaces.why: a large dataframe engine: SIMD, arrow, very deep generics; the biggest workspace here (its rust-toolchain.toml is ignored, rule own-nightly)
